subject: MSA + Order Form — proposed language for output & training use
messages:
From: Mark Olson <olson@stratumhealth.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Roy <aisha.roy@stratumhealth.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — output ownership & training carveouts

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Attached are Stratum's redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. Two items we need to resolve before we can proceed to procurement:

1) Output ownership: we expect the Order Form to explicitly assign "Customer Output" (the text and artifacts produced by the Service from Customer prompts/data) to Stratum.
2) Training/data use: Stratum will not agree to any clause that allows Platform Provider to use Customer-provided inputs or outputs to train base models without an explicit opt-in. We can accept telemetry for operational monitoring (latency, errors) in an anonymized, aggregated form; but not training.

Please review the attached marked-up MSA and the small exhibit showing proposed alternative language. We can be flexible on narrow feedback licenses for product improvement (e.g., bug fixes, non-training quality work) so long as it excludes model re-training or inclusion in a general-purpose model.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: (a) a clause that assigns outputs to Stratum; and (b) a binding commitment that Customer data/outputs won't be used for model training absent opt-in? If you can send proposed language by end of day we can route internally to our legal team. If helpful, Aisha and I can join a short call later today.

Thanks,

Mark Olson
Olson Legal — Counsel to Stratum Health

Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — output ownership & training carveouts

Thanks Mark — received and looping in Laura and Ben from Legal/Commercial. Quick acknowledgement and next steps:

- We can accept explicit assignment of Customer Output to Stratum in the Order Form (narrowly defined).
- For training/data use, Redwood cannot agree to unrestricted use of Customer inputs/outputs to train our base models. We can offer two paths:
  * Opt-in training: Customer may opt in to allow Redwood to use de-identified outputs/inputs for model training for a commercial credit; OR
  * No-training (default): Redwood may only use aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics for operational improvements and bug fixes, and will not incorporate Customer-provided content into public or base models.

Below I've pasted a concise draft snippet for the Order Form / Exhibit that Laura can iterate on. If this captures the approach, we'll send a redline back to you shortly.

--- draft snippet ---
Order Form — Customer Output and Training Use
1. Customer Output: "Customer Output" means text, images, or artifacts produced by the Service in response to Customer prompts or inputs. Customer is granted exclusive ownership of Customer Output, subject to the limited rights set forth below.
2. Feedback and Operational Improvements: Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide right to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry and feedback for the purpose of improving service reliability, diagnostics, and performance.
3. Model Training; Opt-in: Redwood shall not use Customer-provided prompts, inputs, or Customer Output to retrain or augment Redwood's base models or publicly available models without Customer's prior written consent. If Customer elects to opt in to training, the parties will execute a separate Training Addendum that specifies the scope, compensation, and data handling safeguards.
--- end snippet ---

Action items: Laura to run legal redline; Ben to assess procurement/discount implications for opt-in training; I will propose meeting slots for a 30-min legal sync if needed.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — output ownership & training carveouts

Vivek / Laura — quick commercial/legal note from my side:

- I agree with Vivek's two-path approach. From a sales/procurement perspective, customers frequently want explicit output ownership; that's an easy win. The sticking point is the optics on "training" — many enterprise buyers will insist on no-training without compensation.

Suggested compromise language for the Order Form:
- "Customer Output is owned by Customer. Redwood will not use Customer-provided inputs or Customer Output to train or improve any model that is materially available to third parties absent a separate written agreement."
- "Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and system logs for service health and performance improvements; such telemetry will not be added to any training corpus in a way that associates the telemetry with Customer's identity or Customer Output."

Also recommend adding an audit clause for the training opt-in addendum: Stratum can request a one-time attestation (or SOC-type statement) about the types of data used if they opt in. Procurement likes that.

I'll draft a short procurement-friendly redline and hand it to Laura for legal polish. My read: we can converge in 1-2 business days.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference

Mark / Aisha — thanks for the redlines and for outlining Stratum's position. Per internal review, we've put together a consolidated proposal (below) intended to be minimal change to your Order Form while preserving Stratum's principal ask. If this looks acceptable we can produce a clean redline for signature.

Consolidated proposal (high level):
- Affirmative assignment of Customer Output to Stratum (as defined).
- Explicit prohibition on using Customer-provided inputs or Customer Output for model training unless Stratum signs a Training Addendum.
- Redwood retains the right to use aggregated/anonymized telemetry and feedback for operational purposes and non-training product improvements.
- Optional commercial path: if Stratum opts in to training, Redwood will offer a negotiated credit/discount and execute a Training Addendum that defines scope, retention, and security controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura will circulate a redline of the MSA/Order Form reflecting the snippet we sent earlier.
2) Mark / Aisha to review and flag any points that require a call.
3) If needed, propose a 30-min call tomorrow 10:00-10:30am PT — does that work for you?
